text:
The moon rests low on the darkened horizon, dawn only a sliver of light along the east. It's quiet, but for the reassuring rhythmic crashing of the surf 
along the outcroppings of coral that stretch across the sands like fingers pulling the island into the sea. The Traveler loved this time of the night, as if each 
cool breath of air carried the scent of purpose and peace.
 
Then a nagging thought crept in: Sol'Kesh is not peaceful, quiet only means imminent death. The Traveler stopped mid stride and listened. Wind softly 
sifting over the dune grass, birds in the distance singing to the barely risen sun and, between the crash of the waves, a rasping, slithering sound could be 
heard across the sands. With bated breath and a pounding heart, the Traveler silently steps back further inland, past waist-high dune grass and moves 
quickly to a rocky knoll that overlooks the seascape.
Dawn's light soon gives form to the coast and, at the receding tide, a long sinuous shape rises from the black water. Standing taller than the Traveler, a 
slick, nearly bipedal creature lifts its long twin pronged nose to twitch in the cool air and slowly it turns towards the Traveler. Unprepared and unwilling 
to face the looming threat, the Traveler eases back, keeping eyes glued to the dark stalker. The Traveler continues to slowly inch backward, only turning 
when the amphibious killer slithers back under the waves.
Evolved to stalk silently, little escapes this blind amphibian. A long, sensitive, dual-horned nose leads its way when in dark waters, 
sensing the electromagnetic pulse of nearby creatures. Their frightened heartbeats like a call to the slaughter as its long lithe body 
swims silently along the coral strands that twists over and under the waves. Daellash, daugon, even the voracious goliarch, stand little 
chance once this creature has tracked their beating hearts, blood pulsing loudly along the slannethiss' pronged horns as it closes the 
distance. For those believing the shore is safe from its extrasensory abilities, dozens of heat pits line the creature's head, allowing a full 
spectrum of thermal vision to aid this large nocturnal amphibian to dominate wide stretches of the shoreline. When rains pummel 
the coast, muffling the sound of its approach, it ventures further inland for warm blooded prey. Solitary creatures all, when two sense 
another nearby, they will politely draw back to unseen territory lines to keep from each other's presence and dwindling prey. Only in the 
rarest of occasions when too many of the amphibians vie for the same territory will they openly fight, slashing and slamming themselves 
against the other, the victor breaking off the weaker beast's sensory horns, pitying it as it flails in absolute pain and blindness.
Unlike the other apex predators on this isolated island, the presence of the slannethiss brings little balance to its hunting grounds. If 
anything, it upends it so heavily that little more than small fish become all that remains of the animal life within the area. Many believe 
that the slannethiss is not native to the island, or native to an environment above ground, and that may explain why the surrounding 
flora and fauna have simply not had time to adjust to its malevolent presence.
 
This hypothesis rings true when one studies which locations the amphibian prefers to haunt. Coasts open to the sky with long stretches 
of beach give this predator little cover to slink behind; instead, areas rife with caverns, narrow channels and, most favorably, the 
weaving of strands of coral are usually where this beast is found to nest. Many solitary slannethiss can be found in Dawn's Reach, 
for just that reason. With a multitude of islands, their coasts expanded further by long stretches of coral pillars that criss cross over 
each other to the sandy ocean floor, harboring an immense diversity of crustacean and fish that just manages to survive the ravenous 
predator. Further west, among the peninsula of Shatter Mouth, the waters run fast into the hollowed caves that riddle the many islands 
that meet the exit of the Shiverrun river. While not as plentiful as the corals to the east, the seasonal fish spawnings and the aggressive 
rauka that guard the river mouth provide a near endless supply of beasts for the predator to slay.
The cunning salamanders are far from unaware of their devastating impact on the ecosystem. After months of stalking the tides, either 
killing or frightening away any creature worth the effort to hunt soon forces them to migrate. Females will lay clusters of unfertilized 
eggs within deep crevices that face the ocean. These thickly gelled eggs will remain there for seasons, sometimes years, keeping damp 
by the surrounding water and awaiting both the fauna to return to the waters, and for a male to take up residence in the hunting 
ground the female had long since left behind. With electric sensors reading the subtle but telltale sign of awaiting eggs, the males will 
approach, fertilize and soon raise the young until they grow large enough to find their own hunting grounds. Conversely, when females 
chance upon another's eggs, they will quickly tear them apart and replace them with their own.
The shores of Sol'Kesh teem with life: Beaches covered in scuttling crabs, clouds of birds plucking them from the sand and schools of 
darting fish of every color. When a Traveler instead notices a barren absence, they must ready themselves, for they have stepped deep 
within the apex creature's lair. The slannethiss is no brute, it doesn't bellow its dominance to every beast within earshot, it doesn't 
challenge every other predator that steps into its territory, it simply stalks. Unseen until the last moment before it strikes, this stealthy 
hunter will track a Traveler for miles, learn their ways, their routines and attack when they least expect it. The only defense, the only 
way to survive, is to be a sliver more cunning than the amphibian, laying traps or, better yet, leave the coast and walk inland, far from 
the deadly tide.
